f1_5: Anxiety deserves the same kind of listening. A lot of the time it's a part of you that's trying to protect you, making a guess about what's coming: that you'll get overwhelmed, maybe, or that people will laugh at you. It can be right! It's probably been wrong before too, and you know some of those times. So when it's safe to find out, I'd hear it out and then go see. Maybe nobody laughs. (Or they do, and you survive it.) If it might be real danger, though, I'd get some distance first, and find out how right it was later. Same with something a doctor should look at.
d1_5: Your little one will still be there later. Some people want out of the whole inner-child idea, though, and that's a different thing. If that's you, I wouldn't keep sneaking it back in through some "gentler" version, or start calling the dishes reparenting. Looking after yourself and keeping yourself safe can happen in whatever words feel like yours. Same with figuring out where you're headed, and getting support from people.
d2_5: If you do want it, and it's just too much at this depth, I'd go shallower. Some people try one technique after another at that point, as if it's a test they have to pass. If going inward keeps making it worse, or you're not sure you could stop and come back, I'd put the inward stuff down and come back out to the room. Once you're steadier, there's a harm-reduction saying for this: start low and go slow. Low might be doing one protective thing out in your life, or calling someone who's good for you. Or a short hello to your little one with your eyes open.
d3_5: A full pause from your little one is the last thing I'd reach for, but sometimes you need one, for safety or because nothing smaller is working. (Looking after yourself, and seeing the people who are good for you, can keep going.) I'd write down why. Then the last level you could still handle, and what would have to change before you'd go back. Some people keep taking little peeks during a pause, just a quick hello, just a bit of imagery. I'd wait. When that change is there and you want to come back, start at that last level you could handle, or lower.
p2_5: So how were the next few days? How did you sleep, and could you get through your day okay? Do you want to go back toward what came up, or is some part of you saying no? (And could you have stopped and come back to the room, if you'd needed to? If not, I'd keep my eyes open next time, before any imagery.) If you honestly can't tell yet, I wouldn't rush to call it healing or harm. I'd just make the next one a bit easier, one change at a time, so you learn what made the difference. If you're getting worse, though, change several things at once, and have someone steady with you.
i1_5: Maybe part of what your little one went through was being alone with it. Then reaching toward people can be part of this work too, and you can call that reparenting if you like the word. Some people figure they have to finish healing on their own first, and only then will they be fit company for anybody. I don't think a decent parent would ask that of a lonely kid. So sometimes the grown-up thing to do is just to text someone first.
c2_5: And reaching out doesn't mean telling strangers everything. Privacy isn't fakery. People can earn more of you by how they handle the smaller things you tell them, and how they take it when you say no. But if a relationship is getting deep and you're still keeping up a fake normal, happy version of yourself to hold onto it, I'd either bring more of the truth in, carefully, or let it be less deep for now. (If telling could put you in real danger, like violence, or being outed where that isn't safe, protect yourself first.) And when someone finally accepts you, it can feel amazing. It still doesn't prove you're meant for each other, or that they've earned your trust yet.
i2_5: I'd look for more than one place to belong, too. One partner or one therapist can't be all of it, and if they're busy or gone, you'd be left with nobody. Keep the good people you've got, and then maybe add a spiritual community that fits you, or a class you keep showing up to. Not every one of them has to click. But if some group makes you feel more wanted than you've ever felt, while telling you who you shouldn't see anymore, I'd let the Protector handle that one, and keep your other people, even if it means not going back.
